subject: Biotechnology
title: Extremophiles and Astrobiology
description: Learn Extremophiles and Astrobiology in one minute.

hook.text: Tardigrades survive the vacuum of space — extremophiles prove life can endure conditions once thought impossible.

buildup.text: Deinococcus radiodurans survives 5,000 Gy of radiation — it reassembles its shattered genome in hours using backup copies.

discovery.text: Deep-sea vent organisms live without sunlight — chemosynthesis suggests life could exist on Europa or Enceladus.

twist.text: Finding extremophiles on Earth does not prove alien life exists — but it expands the definition of habitable environments.

climax.text: NASA's Mars Sample Return mission will search for biosignatures — molecular evidence of past or present microbial life on Mars.

punchline.text: Earth's extremes breed life — extremophiles widen the search for alien biology.

quiz.question: Why do deep-sea chemosynthetic organisms suggest life could exist on Europa?
options: Europa has the same ocean temperature as Earth's deep seas
Chemosynthesis proves life can exist without sunlight, and Europa's subsurface ocean may have similar chemical energy sources
Deep-sea organisms on Earth originally came from Europa
